title: Zoom in: what the Inventory API does with a key
caption: The claim is one atomic insert-or-take-over. Everything after it is either the single owner doing the work or a cheap answer from the key row.

steps.text: A reserve call arrives with key, SKU and quantity. The API hashes the body so a later request with the same key can be compared.
Claim: insert the key row as in_progress with a short lease. If the row exists but its lease has run out, the claim takes it over instead.
The claim succeeded, so this request is the only one allowed to touch stock for this key.
In the same transaction: write the reservation, decrement available stock, store the reply on the key row and add a stock-reserved outbox row.
Commit and answer 201. From now on the key row alone can answer for this reservation.

scenarios.name: Retry while in progress
scenarios.summary: A retry lands while the first attempt is still working: it gets 409 instead of a second reservation. The next retry, after the commit, gets the stored reply.

steps.text: The first attempt is waiting on a row lock. The order service gives up waiting and retries with the same key and body.
The claim fails: a live lease already owns the key. The body hash matches.
No reply is stored yet, so answer 409 with Retry-After. Nothing waits on the hot row.
The next retry comes after the commit and gets the stored 201, byte for byte.

scenarios.name: Same key, different body
scenarios.summary: A client bug sends a new quantity under an old key. Replaying the old reply would be wrong and so would reserving again; the request is refused.

steps.text: A cart edit reuses the key of an earlier reservation but asks for a different quantity.
The key exists, so the claim fails, and the stored body hash doesn't match the new one.
Answer 422: the caller must use a new key for a new intent. The bug shows up in logs instead of in the stock count.

scenarios.name: Owner dies mid-reserve
scenarios.summary: The instance that claimed the key crashes before committing. Its transaction rolls back, the lease runs out, and a later retry becomes the new owner.

steps.text: The key is claimed and the reservation is being written when the instance is killed.
Nothing was committed, so no stock is held. Retries during the lease still see in_progress and get 409.
After the lease runs out, the next retry's claim takes the key over and does the work once.
